conviction_note: Most of what bears on this print was said by the CFO himself on 2026-09-14: returns at the top end of the range or better, NII top end or better, Markets up mid-single digits, IB up low-single digits, plus about $500m of extra H2 spend. Peer remarks (GS FICC softer, BofA IB down 10-20%, Jefferies fixed income -26%) lean the other way, and the 25-delta skew pays mildly for downside. That leaves a near-balanced lean (p_up 54) on a 4.0% absolute move. The findings sum to about +0.1. Both numbers are small because the guide was pre-announced, not because the move will be small. JPM, WFC and GS report the same morning, before Citi, so the sector tape will drive much of the window.
bar: Q3 2026 EPS of about $2.65-2.68 on revenue of about $23.66-23.76bn. Zacks has $2.66 (revised down over the last 7 days) on $23.66bn: https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/3004113/citigroup-(c)-laps-the-stock-market:-here's-why. FMP has $2.65 on $23.70bn: https://site.financialmodelingprep.com/market-news/citigroup-q3-earnings-preview-estimates-outlook. Hudson Labs has $2.68 on $23,756m: https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/citigroup-q3-2026-earnings-c-revenue-eps-preview. WSJ consensus checked 2026-10-12 is $2.65: https://www.indmoney.com/blog/us-stocks/us-bank-earnings-q3-jpm-bac-gs-wfc-citi-blk-ms-stock-earnings. Several sources agree, and it sits on the company's own Sept 14 guide: FY RoTCE a bit above 11%, efficiency a bit better than 60%, NII ex-Markets +5-6% at the top end or better, Q3 Markets +MSD YoY, Q3 IB +LSD YoY (https://www.citigroup.com/rcs/citigpa/storage/public/2026-citigroup-barclays-global-financial-services-conference-transcript.pdf). print_vs_bar is on revenue; Citi has beaten EPS 8 quarters running and beat Q2 revenue by about 5.5% ($24.77bn vs $23.47bn).
positioning_check: Short interest is light. Equibles shows 24.7M shares short, 1.4% of float, 2.1 days to cover at the 2026-08-19 settlement, down 4.1M (https://equibles.com/stocks/c/shortinterest). shortsqueeze.com shows 28.77M and 2.3 days on 2026-08-03 (https://shortsqueeze.com/?symbol=C). Not a crowded short. Options: 25-delta skew +2.38 vol points (downside paid, mild), put/call OI 1.01, event-implied move 3.80% (straddle 4.18%), ATM IV 45.4%. Tape: 20-day run-up -3.64% (much of it the 2026-09-15 sector sell-off on BofA's IB warning), 5-day +2.08%, 9.9% below the 52-week high.

findings.finding: At the 2026-09-14 Barclays conference the CFO effectively raised the FY2026 guide. RoTCE is now 'a bit above our 11%', against the 10-11% guided in July. Efficiency is 'a bit better than the 60%' (July: around 60%). NII ex-Markets is 'top end of [5-6%] or a bit better'. He cited 'really good momentum in the third quarter'. H1 RoTCE was about 13%, so a FY a bit above 11% implies H2 at about 9.5-10%. Consensus Q3 EPS of $2.66 against Q2's $3.15 implies a Q3 RoTCE of about 10.5%. The bar therefore sits on the guide, and the print is where the July 'unchanged guide' is formally replaced by the raised one.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 (2026-07-14) Citi beat EPS ($3.15) with the FY guide unchanged and 'muddied' H2 spend messaging. The stock fell 5.29% over the window (-4.4% per Kalkine). Q1 2026 +2.61%, Q4 2025 -3.34%, Q3 2025 +3.89%. This name trades on the guide and the expense outlook, not on the beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. It was said publicly four weeks ago, and the stock still fell 1-2% that day with the sector on BofA's warning. What the market has not yet seen is the formal number in the release, or whether the CFO lifts it again given his statement that 'a couple of months have gone by'. If the raise were fully priced, the stock would not be 9.9% below its high with a -3.6% 20-day run-up and puts bid.
findings.independence: The consensus RoTCE-implied arithmetic draws on several preview sources (Zacks, FMP and Hudson Labs, links in bar). Hudson Labs summarises the same transcript, so it is not independent of the source.

findings.finding: Citi is pulling forward about $500m of its $5bn multi-year investment into H2 2026, 'weighted towards severance' plus card and wealth marketing (Barclays, 2026-09-14). On the Q2 call it said 'in some of the next few quarters, we do expect expense growth to outpace revenue growth'. H1 severance was already about $800m ($500m Q1, $300m Q2). Q2 expenses were $14.2bn. The Q3 expense step-up and its split between Q3 and Q4 are not disclosed. The same H2-spend line sold the Q2 beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 traded -5.29% on 'muddied messaging on H2 spend' despite an EPS beat (https://www.fxleaders.com/news/2026/07/15/citigroup-c-stock-price-forecast-citi-slides-as-strong-earnings-fail-to-ease-spending-concerns/).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely inside the guide. The $500m was quantified on Sept 14, and consensus EPS already steps down from $3.15 to about $2.66. The unpriced part is the timing: if most of the severance lands in Q3, the reported efficiency ratio and EPS could look worse than a model that spreads it evenly. If that were priced, consensus would carry a wide range; TickerLeague shows $2.30-2.73.
findings.independence: The Barclays transcript (https://www.citigroup.com/rcs/citigpa/storage/public/2026-citigroup-barclays-global-financial-services-conference-transcript.pdf) is a second company document with the $500m figure. It is the same company voice, so not independent.

findings.finding: Peer read since Citi last spoke is soft on the lines Citi leans on. Jefferies' fiscal Q3 (Jun-Aug, reported 2026-09-28) had fixed income revenue -26% YoY and debt underwriting -21%, while advisory (+25%) and ECM (+69%) were records. Goldman's CEO said on 2026-09-16 that FICC would be 'slightly softer' and IB 'much more muted'. BofA guided Q3 IB fees down 10-20% YoY with trading flat. Citi's Markets is FICC-heavy and its IB leans to DCM, but Citi guided Markets +MSD and IB +LSD on 2026-09-14 with about 2.5 months of the quarter known.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Markets drove the Q1 and Q2 2026 beats (Q2 Markets +17%). The July call warned that the H1-to-H2 Markets decline (historically about 20%) 'could be greater this year'. No resolved print to cite where Markets alone missed.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The sector sold off 2026-09-15 on BofA (C -1-2%), and the Jefferies print came after Citi spoke but covers Jun-Aug only. Citi's own later guide on the same quarter is the more direct series, so this proxy is sized below it. If it were unpriced, C would not already have underperformed 20d (-3.6%).
findings.independence: Goldman CFO/CEO remarks: https://kfgo.com/2026/09/16/goldman-ceo-says-fixed-income-currencies-commodities-business-slightly-softer-in-q3/. BofA warning: https://parameter.io/bank-of-america-bac-slides-5-on-investment-banking-revenue-warning-for-q3/. Three separate counterparties.

findings.finding: The Citibank Credit Card Issuance Trust 10-D for the due period ending 2026-08-26 shows 30+ day delinquency of about 1.29%. That is down from 1.32% in July and from 1.42% a year earlier. The credit-loss component is 2.03% (July 1.90%, June 2.25%). Card credit looks benign into Q3, consistent with U.S. card NCL toward the low end of the 4-4.5% FY guide and room for reserve stability or release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Credit has not been the line Citi traded on in the last four prints. Moves were explained by guide and expense messaging.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The CFO said credit is stable and delinquencies are down YoY on 2026-09-14. The trust is a small (~$19bn), seasoned slice of the card book, so it is a proxy for the reported NCL rather than the number itself.
findings.independence: July 10-D (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001108348/000119312526353756/d138267dex99.htm) and Barclays transcript credit remarks.

findings.finding: The Fed raised rates 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, its first hike since 2023, with a hawkish dot plot. Citi's NII ex-Markets is volume-driven and asset-sensitive, so this supports the 'top end or better' NII guide and a firmer Q4/2027 NII outlook. It is a headwind to AOCI, TBV and CET1 (12.8% vs a 12.6% target). The rate decision source is secondhand.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None specific to Citi in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Macro, public and transmitted through models already. The only unpriced part is whether management quantifies an NII upgrade on the call. If it were fully priced, Visible Alpha's +11% Q3 NII estimate would already include it; the 2026-10-10 Visible Alpha preview shows NIM declining.
findings.independence: Proxy. The CFO said on 2026-09-14 that 'rates around the world [have] an upward bias' (Barclays transcript), but did not quantify it.

findings.finding: JPMorgan and Wells Fargo (about 7:00 ET) and Goldman Sachs (7:30 ET) all report on 2026-10-13 before Citi's 8:00 ET release, so the sector's read of trading and IB will be set before Citi's numbers land, inside the same window. BofA and Morgan Stanley report the following morning, outside the window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-07-14 the same cluster reported the same morning and Citi fell 5.29%.
findings.why_not_priced: The sign cannot be known before the release. It is filed so that judges know a large part of the window's move is sector beta set by three peers' prints.
findings.independence: Calendar also in the sweep row and Citi's own release (https://www.citigroup.com/global/news/press-release/2026/citi-third-quarter-2026-earnings-call).

findings.finding: Capital return. Citi bought back $10.3bn in H1 2026, but the CFO's FY framing is only 'ahead of what we did last year, which was about $13 billion', and he said CET1 (12.8% vs a ~12.6% target) will not make 'very sharp movements'. A Q3 buyback well below the H1 run-rate (~$5bn a quarter) would fit that language, and the Fed hike's AOCI drag makes it more likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved print where the buyback pace alone was the move.
findings.why_not_priced: An inference from wording. A Q3 buyback of about $4bn (the Q2 pace) is plausibly what models carry. If a slowdown were expected, previews would flag it, and none found does.
findings.independence: Shares the Barclays transcript with finding 1. Q2 call: $4bn bought back in Q2, CET1 target about 12.6% (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/21/citi-c-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/).

outside_window.finding: Banamex: Citi now owns about 51% after closing the last 1.4% tranche. Deconsolidation is expected 'early next year' (2027), with an expected CTA loss of about $9bn through the P&L and no impact on regulatory capital or TCE. No further sales in 2026. The call may restate timing, but the event is in 2027.
The September-period card trust 10-D (the third month of Q3) will be filed around 2026-10-15, after the window.

baseline_tension: A mild upward lean from the company's own pre-announced guide raise against mildly bid puts (skew +2.38) and a -3.6% 20-day run-up. The peer FICC/IB softness agrees with the skew, so p_up sits only 4 points above 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (inside what the company guided): the guide-raise finding cut from +0.8 to +0.5 and the expense finding from -0.5 to -0.3, because both were stated publicly on 2026-09-14
Lesson 5 (a company number beats a proxy): the peer-read finding cut from -0.4 to -0.2, because Citi's own later guide on the same quarter is the more direct series
Lesson 5 (proxy and macro transmission): the card-trust finding cut from +0.2 to +0.1 and the Fed-hike finding from +0.2 to +0.1; the buyback inference cut from -0.2 to -0.1
Lesson 1 (reaction veto): left p_up at 54 rather than higher, given the Q2 beat sold -5.3%; abs_move and p_up unchanged, so the sum is unchanged at +0.1
